n: Christ dictates a letter to the church at Ephesus, a large port city and home of the famous temple of Artemis. He presents Himself as the one who holds the leaders and walks among the churches.

f.g: He is present with and watches over His churches.

n: Christ praises their hard work, endurance, and refusal to tolerate evil. They tested people who falsely claimed to be apostles and exposed them.

f.w: say they are apostles, and are not

n: They have endured hardships for Christ’s name and have not grown weary.
But Christ has a concern: they have abandoned the love they had at first. Correct doctrine without love is not enough.
Remember how far you have fallen, repent, and do what you did at first. Otherwise Christ will remove their lampstand—they would cease to be His church.

f.g: Their standing as a light-bearing church would be taken away.

n: Still, they rightly hate the practices of the Nicolaitans, which Christ hates too. The Nicolaitans were apparently a group that compromised with idolatry and immorality.

f.g: A sect whose exact teachings are uncertain; linked with the ‘doctrine of Balaam’ in verses 14-15.

n: Each letter ends with a call to listen and a promise. Whoever overcomes will eat from the tree of life in God’s paradise—access lost in Eden restored.
To Smyrna (modern İzmir), Christ speaks as the One who died and came back to life—fitting for a church facing death.

f.g: A wealthy port city known for loyalty to Rome and emperor worship.

n: Christ knows their suffering and poverty, but says they are truly rich. Some local opponents claim God’s covenant but act as Satan’s assembly by slandering believers.

f.g: A sharp label for local opponents who persecuted the believers.

n: Don’t fear coming suffering. Some will be imprisoned for a short, limited time—“ten days.” Be faithful even to death, and Christ will give you the crown of life.
Those who overcome will not be harmed by the second death—final spiritual separation from God.
To Pergamos, Christ speaks as the One with the sharp two-edged sword. Pergamos was a seat of Roman government, which held the ‘right of the sword’—but Christ’s sword is greater.

f.g: Pergamum, a provincial center of Roman power and emperor worship.

n: They live where “Satan’s seat” is—perhaps the great altar of Zeus or the emperor-worship temple. Yet they stayed loyal even when Antipas was martyred there.
But some follow the “doctrine of Balaam,” who advised King Balak to lure Israel into idolatry and immorality. Similar compromises were creeping in.
Some also hold to the Nicolaitans’ teaching, which Christ hates.
Repent, or Christ will come and fight such teachers with the sword of His word.
Overcomers will receive hidden manna—heavenly food—and a white stone with a new name only the receiver knows. Latter-day Saints connect the white stone to a Urim and Thummim given to celestial heirs.
To Thyatira, a trade city famous for guilds, Christ speaks as the Son of God with eyes of fire and feet of bronze.

f.g: A city of trade guilds; Lydia the seller of purple came from here.

n: Christ commends their love, service, faith, and endurance—and notes they are doing even more now than at first.

f.w: the last to be more than the first
f.g: Their recent works exceed their earlier ones.

n: But they tolerate a woman, nicknamed “Jezebel” after Ahab’s idolatrous queen, who claims to be a prophetess and leads people into immorality and idol feasts.
Christ gave her time to repent, but she refused.
Her bed of sin will become a bed of suffering, and her followers will face great distress unless they repent.

f.g: A bed of sickness or affliction.

n: Her spiritual children will die, and all the churches will know Christ searches minds and hearts and repays each by their works.

f.g: Kidneys—seat of deepest feelings and thoughts.

n: To the faithful in Thyatira who rejected this teaching and the so-called “deep secrets of Satan,” Christ adds no further burden.

f.g: Perhaps the false teachers boasted of ‘deep’ knowledge.

n: Just hold on to what you have until He comes.
Whoever overcomes and keeps Christ’s works to the end will share His authority over the nations.
He will rule with an iron scepter, shattering resistance like pottery, just as Christ received from His Father. The JST renders this as ruling with the word of God.
Christ will also give him the morning star—Christ Himself.
Listen to what the Spirit is saying to the churches—these messages apply to us too.
